In Scottish Gaelic, claidheamh mòr means great sword. The two-handed Highland sword of that name was used in clan warfare from the late Middle Ages into the 1600s. Its crossguard angles toward the blade and ends in quatrefoil ornaments.

Later the word was also applied to the basket-hilted Highland broadsword, so older writing can mean either weapon.
